items.q: First line maintenance therapy for moderate allergic rhinitis is what?
o: Daily intranasal corticosteroid with correct technique
items.exp: Intranasal steroids control all allergic symptoms including congestion best and are first line maintenance; antihistamines adjunct for itch and sneeze. Chronic decongestant causes rebound medicamentosa.
r: Incorrect. Antihistamine alone undercontrols congestion.
Correct. Daily intranasal steroid is backbone.
Incorrect. Indefinite decongestant causes rhinitis medicamentosa.
Incorrect. Antibiotics do not treat allergy.
items.kp: Nasal steroid daily beats all comers in allergy.

items.q: Rebound congestion after months of topical decongestant spray is called what?
items.exp: Prolonged vasoconstrictor use down regulates receptors causing rebound hyperaemia and spray dependence (rhinitis medicamentosa), treated by stopping spray with intranasal steroid cover.
r: Incorrect. Allergy has itch and trigger pattern without spray dependence.
Correct. Spray induced rebound is medicamentosa.
Incorrect. Atrophic rhinitis crusts with foetor and wide cavities.
Incorrect. It worsens, not cures, vasomotor symptoms.
items.kp: Addicted nose spray creates its own blockage.

items.q: Pale painless insensate grape like masses in middle meatus bilaterally are what?
items.exp: Ethmoid polyps are oedematous pale prolapses, bilateral and insensate, distinguishing them from pink sensitive turbinates which should never be biopsied or removed as polyps.
r: Incorrect. Turbinates are pink, sensitive and fixed.
Correct. Bilateral pale grapes are polyps.
Incorrect. Antrochoanal is solitary from maxillary sinus.
Incorrect. Haematoma is septal boggy swelling post trauma.
items.kp: Pale and numb equals polyp; pink and tender equals turbinate.

items.q: Samter triad comprises nasal polyps, asthma and sensitivity to what?
items.exp: Aspirin exacerbated respiratory disease combines polyps, asthma and NSAID respiratory reactions from arachidonic shunting to leukotrienes; aspirin desensitisation helps selected specialist cases.
r: Incorrect. Penicillin allergy is separate drug reaction.
Correct. Aspirin and NSAID sensitivity completes triad.
Incorrect. Pollen drives seasonal rhinitis.
Incorrect. Mite drives perennial allergy without triad.
items.kp: Polyps, wheeze and aspirin do not mix.

items.q: Single unilateral polyp in a 16 year old arising through choana most likely is what?
items.exp: Antrochoanal polyps grow singly from maxillary antrum through accessory ostium into choana in adolescents, causing unilateral obstruction and requiring surgical removal with antral widening. Inverted papilloma favours older adults.
r: Incorrect. Ethmoid polyps are bilateral adult disease.
Correct. Solitary choanal polyp of youth is antrochoanal.
Incorrect. Papilloma is older adult lateral wall tumour.
Incorrect. Angiofibroma bleeds vascularly in males.
items.kp: One polyp through back of young nose: antrochoanal.

items.q: Chronic rhinosinusitis duration threshold is symptoms beyond how long?
items.exp: Twelve weeks of nasal blockage, discharge, facial pain or smell loss (two or more, one being blockage or discharge) defines chronic rhinosinusitis, versus acute viral (under 10 days) and acute bacterial patterns.
r: Incorrect. Two weeks is prolonged acute course.
Correct. Twelve weeks makes it chronic.
Incorrect. Three days is common cold onset.
Incorrect. Year overshoots definition.
items.kp: Twelve weeks of sinus symptoms equals chronic.

items.q: Severe recurrent polyps with asthma failing steroids and surgery may receive specialist therapy with what class?
o: Biologics targeting type 2 inflammation (IgE, IL4, IL5 pathways)
items.exp: Monoclonal biologics against IgE, IL4 receptor or IL5 pathways shrink type 2 polyps and reduce surgery and steroid need in selected severe patients under specialist criteria.
r: Incorrect. Antibiotics do not modify polyp biology.
Correct. Type 2 biologics for severe polyps.
Incorrect. Decongestants worsen mucosa long term.
Incorrect. Cautery treats bleeding points, not polyps.
items.kp: When polyps keep returning, block type 2 signals.

items.q: Intranasal steroid spray technique should aim the nozzle how and why?
o: Outward laterally to avoid septal irritation and bleeding
items.exp: Aiming laterally (same hand to same nostril pointing out, or opposite hand technique per teaching) coats turbinates and avoids septal crusting, epistaxis and perforation from chronic septal jet.
r: Incorrect. Septal jet causes bleeding and perforation.
Correct. Aim outward to turbinates.
Incorrect. Upward wastes dose and irritates.
Incorrect. Crossed aiming still hits septum if pointed in.
items.kp: Spray out, not at the septum.

items.q: Allergen immunotherapy is best reserved for which allergic rhinitis patients?
o: Severe disease with proven dominant allergen failing pharmacotherapy
items.exp: Immunotherapy modifies IgE disease over years for severe patients with demonstrable dominant allergen (pollen, mite) inadequately controlled or intolerant of drugs, after specialist assessment for asthma stability.
r: Incorrect. Controlled mild disease needs no years of injections.
Correct. Severe proven allergen disease failing drugs.
Incorrect. Infants are not candidates.
Incorrect. No allergen means no immunotherapy target.
items.kp: Years of shots only for severe proven allergy.

items.q: Unilateral nasal mass in 60 year old with epistaxis needs exclusion of which lesions first?
items.exp: One sided masses in older adults include inverted papilloma (locally invasive, malignant potential) and squamous carcinoma, mandating imaging and endoscopic biopsy pathway unlike bilateral benign polyps.
r: Incorrect. Bilateral polyps do not explain unilateral mass.
Correct. Papilloma and cancer must be excluded.
Incorrect. Turbinate swelling is mucosal and shrinks.
Incorrect. Rhinitis causes no unilateral mass.
items.kp: One sided mass in older nose: tumour until proven otherwise.
